title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 36, and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, Lead India's First Batch Into Christchurch
excerpt: Five players and the full support staff have landed in New Zealand ahead of the October 22 T20I opener, at the start of a six-week, three-format tour.
body:
• The first batch of India's tour party — five players and the full support staff — has landed in Christchurch ahead of the five-match T20I series against New Zealand starting October 22.
  • The batch spans a generation: Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 36, is its senior-most player; Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, the youngest Indian ever to play international cricket, is its youngest.
  • Jasprit Bumrah has been rested for the T20I series; Shreyas Iyer captains the 16-member squad with Tilak Varma as vice-captain.
  • The full tour runs nearly six weeks: five T20Is to November 1, five ODIs from November 4, and two Tests closing the trip in Wellington and Christchurch.

India's long tour of New Zealand has begun. The first batch of five players, travelling with the full support staff, touched down in Christchurch ahead of the five-match T20I series that opens at Hagley Oval on October 22 and runs to November 1, CricTracker reported. The rest of the 16-member squad announced by the BCCI on October 6 follows in subsequent batches.

"India's long tour of New Zealand has begun."

A study in contrasts

No pairing captures this squad's generational span like its oldest and youngest travellers. Bhuvneshwar Kumar's selection marks a return to T20I cricket after a gap of nearly four years — his last match-winning spell for India in the format came against the same opposition in Napier on November 22, 2022 — though he recently reappeared in the fifth T20I against the West Indies. Across 87 T20Is he has taken 90 wickets at an average of 23.10 and an economy rate of 6.96, with best figures of 5 for 4 and two five-wicket hauls; across all formats he has 294 wickets in 229 internationals.

https://x.com/RevSportzGlobal/status/2112030763512434752

At the other end of the age curve, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his T20I debut against England in July 2026, becoming the youngest Indian to play international cricket and breaking a record long held by Sachin Tendulkar. He arrives in New Zealand with 246 runs from eight T20Is, having finished the Zimbabwe series as its leading scorer with 151 runs and the Player of the Series award — including a 19-ball fifty, the youngest half-century in men's international cricket, and 81 off 49 balls in the final match.

The tour ahead

Shreyas Iyer captains the T20I side, with Tilak Varma as his deputy, and Jasprit Bumrah rested for the series. The T20Is move from Christchurch (October 22 and 24) to Wellington (October 27), Auckland (October 30) and Hamilton (November 1). The ODI squad travels separately on October 28, with the one-day series opening at Eden Park, Auckland on November 4; Shubman Gill leads the ODI side for the first three matches before Iyer takes over, and Gill also captains the two-Test series that closes the tour in Wellington (from November 19) and Christchurch (from November 27), according to the tour programme reported by CricketNews. Diaspora fans in New Zealand get five weeks of it — our commentary and how-to-watch guide has the broadcast details for every match.
